items.title: AI may not improve patient outcomes for stroke
items.excerpt: RSNA 2026 preview: Northwell/Hofstra compared 876 acute ischemic stroke patients before and after five AI tools went live at a comprehensive stroke center; after propensity matching, AI did not change odds of good functional outcome or discharge disposition, though CTA-within-60-minutes rose sharply.

items.title: DL model cuts patient gadolinium exposure to 10% of standard dose
items.excerpt: RSNA 2026 preview: Subtle Medical's deep-learning algorithm restored brain MRI contrast enhancement from a 10% gadolinium dose; in 63 patients, blinded randomized reads found no significant difference in lesion categorization vs. standard-dose images.

items.title: Thyroid ultrasound AI yields high agreement with radiologists
items.excerpt: RSNA 2026 preview: See-Mode thyroid ultrasound AI deployed at 297 U.S. clinics; across 95,000+ studies and 187,000+ nodules (Sep 2025-Apr 2026), radiologists left AI-generated descriptors and TI-RADS level unchanged in nearly 89% of nodules.

items.title: Tele-Cranio: a CT-free AI solution for remote diagnosis and planning of craniomaxillofacial deformities
items.excerpt: npj Digital Medicine: Tele-Cranio is an AI system that enables remote, CT-free assessment and surgical planning for craniomaxillofacial deformities, cutting repeated in-hospital CT and radiation burden, particularly for children.

items.title: Multicenter evaluation of radiomics and multimodal artificial intelligence for colorectal cancer diagnosis and survival prediction
items.excerpt: npj Digital Medicine: two-center retrospective study of 879 participants (741 locally advanced colorectal cancer, 138 benign lesions) combining clinical, radiomic and multimodal AI features for preoperative classification and survival prediction.

items.title: Dual chain-of-thought AI-PDCA framework for clinical history taking and documentation
items.excerpt: npj Digital Medicine: an LLM-based training framework with dual chain-of-thought reasoning and plan-do-check-act feedback for teaching medical students clinical history-taking and documentation.

items.title: Epic Systems defends competitive practices, promises to let AI access its records
items.excerpt: At HLTH, executives from Epic, the largest EHR vendor, defended its competitive practices and pledged to let outside AI tools access patient records held in its systems.

items.title: HLTH26: Where Viz.ai, NRHA's AI collab is making headway
items.excerpt: Seven months into Viz.ai's collaboration with the National Rural Health Association, Viz.ai's chief clinical officer outlines how its AI disease-detection and care-coordination platform is being extended to rural hospitals.

items.title: Medicare Pays For the AI Eye Scan — Nobody Pays For What Comes Next
items.excerpt: MedCity Influencers op-ed: Medicare reimburses autonomous AI diabetic eye exams, but follow-up care for patients the AI flags is not funded, limiting the real-world impact of AI retinopathy screening.

items.title: Abridge Announcements during HLTH Emphasize Growing Healthcare Trend
items.excerpt: Abridge's HLTH announcements reflect the push to bring clinical information and AI documentation into the workflows providers already use.

items.title: Who Should Make Medical-Necessity Decisions: AI, Insurers or Treating Physicians?
items.excerpt: Commentary on insurers' use of AI in medical-necessity and prior-authorization decisions versus treating-physician judgment.

items.title: AI is coming for primary care
items.excerpt: At HLTH, executives debated AI that lets primary care doctors manage far more patients or replaces them, after Oura's plan to acquire AI-based primary care company Counsel Health.

items.title: Development and validation of a machine learning model to predict outpatient appointment non-attendance: a retrospective study using multisource NHS data
items.excerpt: BMJ Open: an appointment-level ML model built on multisource NHS records predicts outpatient 'did not attend' risk to enable targeted interventions that reduce missed appointments.

items.title: Domain-specific large language models with chain-of-thought prompting for antibiotic prescribing: a 2x2 factorial evaluation
items.excerpt: BMJ Health & Care Informatics: compares a domain-specific medical LLM with a general-purpose LLM, with and without chain-of-thought prompting, on how rational and safe their antibiotic prescribing decisions are, plus an LLM-based auto-scorer.
